description: Fixture for selecting records and copying them. Every shape the two copy buttons have to render is here once: a title field (name) and a candidate subtitle (role), a self-identifying identifier that resolves to a link (orcid), a URL long enough to be collapsed to a label on screen but which must arrive whole in the text copy (homepage), a picture column that becomes the thumbnail (photo), a long text field with an embedded newline that must not survive as a line break (bio), a boolean, a number, an empty field that no copy may mention (empty), an array of scalars (tags) and an array of objects (works).

people.name: Ada Lovelace
people.bio:
She worked on the Analytical Engine and wrote what is generally taken to be the first algorithm intended to be carried out by a machine, together with
notes running to three times the length of the memoir they annotate.

people.name: Grace Hopper
people.bio:
She built the first compiler and argued that a programming language could read like English, which is roughly how COBOL came about; she also spent decades
persuading the Navy that a computer need not be a single large machine.

people.name: Alan Turing
people.bio:
He gave a definition of computability in terms of an abstract machine, worked on the wartime decryption of Enigma traffic, and later asked whether the
question of whether a machine can think is a well posed one at all.
